title: UML3 to networking and cloud infrastructure
description: Can a UML3 model describe a deployable infrastructure - a configurable topology on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, or on traditional hardware with routers and firewalls - well enough to generate it and to reason about it? UML3Components already has nodes, devices, execution environments, communication paths and deployment, which is the UML 2.x deployment vocabulary. The rows below are what a cloud or network engineer additionally needs, and most of them are gaps: this is the least covered area of UML3.

coverageLegend.COVERED: a UML3 construct expresses it; the construct is named in the UML3 column
coverageLegend.PARTIAL: expressible, but with loss - the note says what is lost
coverageLegend.GAP: no UML3 construct expresses it; a requirement is needed if it matters
coverageLegend.TBD: not yet analyzed, or the provider's model has not been confirmed

versionBasis: Provider columns name the service that plays each role rather than an API version, because the roles are stable while the APIs are not. Nothing here has been executed: no cloud account or network device was contacted, and the only infrastructure tool on this machine is Docker 29.2.0. Treat every provider cell as analysis to be confirmed by someone who runs that platform.

rows.notes: #device is the hardware, #node the general computational resource, which is the UML 2.x distinction.
Example 02 models exactly this: an image artifact manifesting a component, deployed to an execution environment on a node.
A function is an operation deployed without a durable host; the model can say where it runs but not that it has no host, nor its trigger, timeout or cold-start behaviour.
Multiplicity on a part could state how many, but nothing states a minimum, a maximum or the signal that scales between them. Same gap the language map found for containers.
Nothing says how to tell whether a deployed component is alive, which every orchestrator requires.
A node has no capacity and a deployment no resource request, so nothing can be checked for fit.
The UML 2.x communication path: which nodes can talk. It carries no protocol or address.
There is no construct for an address range, a CIDR block, or the containment of a subnet in a network - the first thing any cloud topology declares.
Placement drives both latency and failure independence, and cannot be stated. A rack and a fault domain are the same idea on premises.

rows.concept: Port and protocol on an endpoint
rows.notes: A port says a service is offered and its interface says what is offered; the transport, the port number and the scheme are not expressible, so nothing can be generated or checked against a firewall rule.
The single most important gap for security review: nothing states who may reach what. A communication path says a link exists, not that traffic on a port is permitted in one direction.
A load balancer is a node that fans traffic to replicas by rule; without replicas or ports it cannot be modeled meaningfully.
A router is a device and #boundary marks an edge, so the topology is drawable; routing tables, next hops and address translation are not expressible.
Nothing gives a deployed service a name that clients resolve, although that name is what every client configuration contains.
A communication path between sites is the right shape; whether the encryption and tunnelling properties should be metadata or a new construct has not been analyzed.
The database and its technology are modelable, and the schema is modelable in UML3Data, but the instance class, storage, backup policy and failover are not.
A bucket is neither a node nor a database; it is a storage service with a name, a region and an access policy, and none of that is expressible.
UML3Messaging covers the brokered topology; retention, partitions and delivery guarantees are not expressed.
The same gap the language map found. A deployment that cannot be configured cannot be promoted between environments, which is the whole point of a configurable deployment.
Sensitivity marks data that needs protection; a secret as a deployable thing with a store, a rotation period and a consumer is not modeled.

One model should describe several environments that differ in size and configuration. Nothing expresses that variation, although SysML v2 variation points may be the right mechanism - worth a requirement rather than a new library.
Which component may call which service, and as whom, is unmodelable. With the firewall gap above this means a UML3 model cannot answer a security question about a deployment.
Nothing states what a component emits or what threshold matters, so an operable deployment cannot be generated from the model alone.

Given the gaps above, no useful Terraform or Bicep can be generated today. This row is the summary of the annex: the deployment vocabulary UML3 inherited from UML 2.x describes a topology, not a configurable infrastructure, and closing it is a library of its own - a candidate UML3Infrastructure beside UML3Components.
